Messages.Author: legbiter
Messages.Body:
i just wanted to remind people of the above quote from William of
Occam, because i think it's relevant to some recent discussion here
about a deck [Rehlow's combo] and a card [Meddling of Semsith]. i've
played with and extensively-tweaked the Combo, and Michael has played
with Meddling of Semsith, and we really don't see what the evidence is
for either the deck or the card being a Threat To VTES As We Know It.
If and when combo decks or Meddling decks start to make things really
boring for everyone we can think about knee-capping them. But i don't
think this will be necessary - counter-strategies will evolve [some
already exist]. In the absence of any evidence that these things are
too powerful IN REAL PLAY, there CERTAINLY isn't an argument for
banning/neutering them NOW.

Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:
"The Emperor" <theem...@chello.se> wrote in message
news:MWP78.4$g7.1...@news01.chello.se...

>
> How many of your decks routinely use more than 7 cards during your turn?
> Those that do will suffer from MoS and might consider some defense against
> it but this is Jyhad where every deck will have some weakness.
>

A more appropriate question is: How many of your decks routinely use at
least one card during your turn that you drew during that turn. And the
answer for me (and most people I've played against) is nearly all of them.
On top of that: How many of your decks routinely use at least one card
during an opponent's turn that you drew during that turn? The answer to
that is, generally, all of the ones that don't answer yes to the first
question.

MoS is wrong because it is obviously more destructive than any other vote
card. It has an extremely unbalanced cost/effect ratio, similar to the
pre-reprint Banishment. Pre-reprint Banishment would effectively make one
minion useless for each time it was played, until you paid enough pool to
re-influence him. MoS will effectively make all minions but one useless
until you can get rid of it (which, face it, you can't).

Messages.Author: Steve Wampler
Messages.Body:
legbiter wrote:



Well, I for one don't need to see what effect it has on actual play to
know that it has an effect which is inappropriate for the game, and thus
should never have been printed. Just like the old Thoughts Betrayed,
which was a little too expensive to be a real game winner, the point is
not wether it is balanced, it is that it's power should not be included
in the game, at any cost or under any circumstances.
A vtes hand is not like a hand in any other ccg. It was never intended
to be a limited resource as in magic or other slow-draw card advantage
games. The rules could have you draw up to hand size once per turn, a la
shadowfist, but they don't. Because the game is designed so that you
have a full hand at all times. Even the cards which can force an
opponent to discard allow redrawing.
And yes, there are defenses. Delaying Tactics is an excellent card in
general, for example. But does the existance of Delaying Tactics mean
that it is ok to print a card which says "Political Action. All
kindred. Worth 1 vote. Your prey is ousted"?

-Steve Wampler

I have to agree about MoS. It will definately slow a deck down. The
biggest targets are of course, card-intensive combat decks. I had MoS
played on my Brujah-Anti vote deck this past weekend, and saw little to no
change in how my deck played. I had to rethink about the cards in my hand
(played a forced awakening on my grandprey's turn, and discarded a master or
two I would've rather kept). If anything, MoS will promote the use of
permanents like weapons or intercept locations, since once they're out, they
don't require a card in hand to use.

still rather have a MoS played on me than 3+ Agressive tactics or 7 raptors.
Hell, I'd rather MoS than have a Camarilla Threat in play. At least MoS
doesn't cost you pool to attempt to cycle.

I disagree. Perhaps the *intent* of bloodlines was to get people to change the
way they construct decks or play the game, but if so then this was a failure.
With the exception of the Blood Brothers, the bloodlines set did very little to
advance the meta-game. The reason for this, quite simply, is that the cards
weren't especially powerful, at least not in deck changing ways. The small
number of vampires with each of the new disciplines and the lack of skill cards
made it not particularly worthwhile to add bloodlines cards to existing deck
concepts nor to play the bloodlines as standalone (which they were never
intended to do). Hence, no effect on the metagame.

>
> Remeber that the game is about fun and creativity... My opinion is
> that WW is trying to get that back into the game.

I more get the impression that WW is trying to make it more like the RPG,
ignoring the fact that it is a different game in its own right, and that things
that work in the RPG don't work well in VTES.
For example, the samed in the RPG are pretty badass. So if there was a group of
nosferatu running around whupping up on people, and a samedi joined them, they
would be even more scary. This is because in the RPG each character has a set
of powers which are internal to that character. However, in the card game
vampiric disciplines only do things when combined with library cards. This
means that simply adding a samedi vampire to a crypt will do nothing to help
it-- than cards must also be added to the library. This will in turn mean that
there will be times when the player will have than cards in hand and no samedi,
or samedi in play and no cards they can play. Thus, adding the samedi reduces
the effectiveness of the deck. This is simply an effect of how the game works.

-Steve Wampler

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Curevei wrote:
>>I think what WW is trying to do is change the game, probably to keep it from
getting stale.>>

This card does not change thegame and keep it from getting stale. It gives
already viable vote decks an *incredibly* overpowered weapon in their already
perfectly acceptable arsenal. How does this card change strategy? Oh, wait--now
*every* deck in the game needs to pack 10 Delaying Tactics in it. I forget,
that is *always* good for a game that every deck needs to contain the same
cards to defend against an overpowered strategy.

>>Sure, this is conceptually bad if you keep playing the same decks.>>

It is bad for every deck ever. The very basis of the game system is the
constant renewal of your expendable resources (your hand). This card takes that
away from a single player selectively, for very little cost. There is *no* deck
that will not suffer horrendously at the hands of this card.

>>But, is it bad in the long run if people start building decks differently?
Won't know for quite a while.>>

How are you going to build a deck differently to work under the treat of this
card? Include 10 Delaying Tactics in every deck you build? Build every deck to
have constant vote lock? Yes, that is good that we have introduced a card that
will *reduce* the number of viable strategies, rather than increase them.

Madness. Madness, I say.

Peter D Bakija

>How are you going to build a deck differently to work under the treat of this
>card? Include 10 Delaying Tactics in every deck you build? Build every deck
>to
>have constant vote lock? Yes, that is good that we have introduced a card
>that
>will *reduce* the number of viable strategies, rather than increase them.

People have already brought up playing with more permanents. Note that playing
more permanents also "defeats" milling strategies.

Alternatively, any way of deck building that reduces a dependency on playing a
large number of cards becomes relatively better. For instance, I see no point
in Read the Winds existence. All it does, essentially, is roll two cards into
one and cost a blood for balance, which isn't useless just redundant. With
cards like Semsmith around, it becomes more useful to play cards like RtW.

There's also playing more vote in your deck to vote it out of existence. If
everyone has more votes, the chances of a multiplayer effort to get rid of it
increases.

One feature of V:TES I decry at times (though not here) is how much a lot of
good decks completely ignore some of the arenas in the game. For instance,
quite a few decks have no votes. WW's long term plan may be to try and move
decks towards toolboxing.

I've seen sets spoiled a small number of cards at a time before. People often
think that some card is God's gift to creation when it gets spoiled only to
realize later that the set as a whole changes the game such that it isn't a big
deal. Now, this is a bit of an orphan card, so it's a slightly different
situation. But, it's theoretically possible that players can adapt now and/or,
by the time it comes out in its set, the game will be played differently enough
that the card isn't unbalanced.

The fact of the matter is, until people show that the card is broken in actual
play, I don't expect WW to do anything about it nor should they.

If all decks must toolbox extensively, then all decks become the same. You
need vote defense, and combat defense, and bleed defense. Then you need to
have stealth, and intercept, and untap. Next, you need to be able to pass
votes to take stuff out, and you need to have permanents. So, everybody
ends up playing Malks again, with all the same permanents and 10 Wakes.
Yippee.

I've already gotten sick of seeing every single deck packing Wakes. I'd
love to see Sleeping Mind (superior) errata'd back to hosing them over. If
*every* deck has to pack everything, it's just not going to be interesting
to play anymore. "What're you playing?" "Lasombra toolbox. You?" "Malkav
toolbox.... My friend here is playing !Malk toolbox." "Ooh... haven't seen
one of those in a while!"

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Curevei wrote:
>>People have already brought up playing with more permanents. Note that
playing
more permanents also "defeats" milling strategies.>>

Playing with permanents simply does not make this card less damaging. What are
you going to do with those permanents without transient resources to back them
up? Bleed for 2 with a laptop at zero stealth? Shoot someone for 1 with a .38?
Get Immortally Grappled at close range with your flame thrower 'cause you
couldn't draw a manuver?

Permanents are handy in the face of this card, sure, but will they make you
actually survive being the ass end of this card? No--you are still going to
die, 'cause you still can only take one viable action per turn, permanents or
no.

>>There's also playing more vote in your deck to vote it out of existence. If
everyone has more votes, the chances of a multiplayer effort to get rid of it
increases.>>

Yes--this pushes a currently very varied game environment in a direction where
all decks look the same. All decks must have a lot of votes. All decks must
have mutliple Delaying Tactics. Intercept isn't neccessary, however--this card
is powerful enough that it will always be worth getting torporized to play it.

>>One feature of V:TES I decry at times (though not here) is how much a lot of
good decks completely ignore some of the arenas in the game.>>

Why is that a problem that needs fixing? Every deck that ignores a certain
arena of the game suffers from built in weakness. Not having votes in your
deck, for instance, leaves you vulnerable to vote decks, which up till now was
enough of a penalty. Why do they need to be further punished?

>>For instance, quite a few decks have no votes. WW's long term plan may be to
try and move decks towards toolboxing.>>

Why? So all decks look the same? Every deck has votes, intercept, bleed,
combat, whatever? How is this good? How is it a good idea to take an
environment where countless different strategies are currently viable and
forceably mash them into a mold so that all decks look the same?

>>I've seen sets spoiled a small number of cards at a time before. People
often
think that some card is God's gift to creation when it gets spoiled only to
realize later that the set as a whole changes the game such that it isn't a big
deal. Now, this is a bit of an orphan card, so it's a slightly different
situation. But, it's theoretically possible that players can adapt now and/or,
by the time it comes out in its set, the game will be played differently enough
that the card isn't unbalanced.>>

There is no way for this card to not be unbalanced. The effect (removing from
your prey the ability to redraw cards during their turn, the major engine of
game play, effectively limiting them to 1 effective action per turn) is in no
way justified by the cost (passing a vote and losing one card slot from your
hand). It has nothing to do with adaptation or game play.

This card is in every significant way comperable to Return to Innocence--a card
that had too little of a cost for its massive destabilizing effect. Return to
Innocence was banned from tournament play. Sure, you could defend against
RtI--play with lots of deflections, use Archon Investigation, whatever, but it
was still deemed inappropriate from competetive play, and thus banned.

Yet here we are again, in a very similar situation. How was it that this card
was introduced in the first place?

>>The fact of the matter is, until people show that the card is broken in
actual
play, I don't expect WW to do anything about it nor should they.>>

All you have to do to show that it is broken in play is simply to call it and
pass it. You prey becomes incapable of playing the game, due to one, incredibly
undercosted card.

That WW let this card come into existance (as a *promo* none the less--don't
you remember the madness back when Precidence released Secrets of Success?) is
an absolute travesty.



Actual rule: only untapped minions can block.
Sleeping Mind: tapped minions cannot block.
Wakey: this vampire can block as if untapped.

Result: Wakey "beats" Sleeping Mind.

The counter-intuitiveness only comes from the fact that Sleeping Mind
restated the existsing rule with players expecting card text to add to
the existing ruleset.

Solution: reprint Sleeping Mind so that the portion that merely
restates the existing rule is omitted to avoid such confusion.

Now, this is not to say that the designer(s) of the card didn't
intend for Sleeping Mind to beat Wake. It only says that the execution
of the card (text) failed to do so. The (presumed) intent would
(probably) have been restored if doing so wouldn't (possibly)
unbalance the card. So no errata was issued to achieve "designer
intent".

> > Wakey overcomes the standard rule -> it overcomes the restatement of
> > the standard rule (since restating it doesn't change anything).
> >
> Yes, but so does the sleeping mind - since both cards break the rule
> how come the wake has precedence over sleeping mind?

Card text. The woken vampire is able to block as if untapped.
Sleeping Mind doesn't prevent the vampire from blocking if he were
untapped, so allows Wake to function (just like Wake is allowed to
function in general despite the requirement that the vampire be
untapped to block as stated in the rules).

"LSJ" <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote in message

> Chris Berger wrote:

>
> A clarification, you mean.
> Counter-intuitive only in that you expect card text to do something other
> than remind you of a standard rule. See the recent thread on Distraction.
>

When a clarification actually changes the way a card is played (and Sleeping
Mind *did* override Wake before the "clarification" was made, as the intent
of the card was obvious and few people examined it closely enough to see
that *technically* it might not work that way if you read the card just
right), I find it hard to not call it errata, or at least a ruling.

> Without internet, some people are "left out in the cold" anyhow (except
> for the reprints and access to local princes).
>
> Those with internet have the online card text and google to add to
> those resources.
>

Then why have rulings list and Card Migrations list at all? People can just
read every single card's text and search google for rulings on every single
card, whether a question comes up on it or not.

The rulings and migrations lists are resources for finding out what's
changed. It's even reasonable to print them out and have them as a resource
for those without internet access (haven't met a VTES player yet who doesn't
but I'm sure there are a number of them out there). It's not reasonable to
print out USENET. At some point, there was a clarification in the rulings
list that said that Sleeping Mind (sup) did not prevent a minion from Waking
and blocking. Then, the text was changed to reflect this, and the
clarification was removed. For some reason, the text change was not added
to the Card Migrations. Sure, the effect is the same as it used to be, but
now all trace of that effect has vanished, for anyone who doesn't have a new
copy of the card (there would not normally be any reason to search google
for rulings on the card... if there hasn't been any change to card text or
any ruling on a card, then it must play as written, right?).

Wouldn't it make things more clear if there were either:
a) Card Migration text that said something like "extra line removed, as it
was ruled to have no effect"., OR
b) a "ruling" that said something like "tapped minions who are allowed to
block "as though untapped" are not prevented from blocking by the superior
line. The most recent printing reflects this."
